name: Skills and procedural memory
summary: Agent skills served from the brain, skills learned from repeated work, and procedural memory of how things get done.

features.name: Skill library
features.summary: Lists and serves shipped and vault-local agent skills and offers the relevant ones for the current turn.
capabilities: Finds SKILL.md folders in shipped `skills/` and the machine's own skills folder; local copies shadow shipped
`list_skills` returns each skill's name, one-line description, path and the same-named copies it shadowed
`get_skill` returns SKILL.md or a named auxiliary file inside that skill's folder; a path cannot escape it
`skills_attach` scores skills on the turn text with BM25 (name 3x, description 1x): top 3 within 1,200 chars
Drops matches that rest only on terms more than half the skills share
Stays off until `skill_auto_attach` is set
An optional `skills` decision-model use (shadow or enforce) picks finalists from the BM25 shortlist
The `open-second-brain` skill teaches the memory layout, default workflow, search surfaces and safety rules
limits: `skills_attach` runs only when an agent or a host provider calls it; no hook injects skills by itself
The decision-model stage only trims or reorders the BM25 shortlist; it never offers a skill outside it

features.name: Skill proposals and rewrites
features.summary: Proposes skills from repeated work and mature pages, and gates skill rewrites on a frozen benchmark.
capabilities: `learn` scans new continuity records for repeated actions, shapes, co-occurrences and daily routines
Drafts a proposal once a pattern has 3 supporting records (2 at least); a verifier checks its evidence
`page-candidates` admits core, fresh, high-confidence pages with observed reuse that no skill covers
`page-draft` stages the agent's draft as a pending proposal; nothing reaches the skills root until accepted
Writes an accepted proposal through a write-ahead journal that `recover` rolls back or forward
`rewrite-plan` verifies a skill's task set against its frozen receipt and prints the two round envelopes
`rewrite-score` grades transcripts structurally: promote, hold or not_enough_evidence, then one held-out check
Accepts a `scored_rewrite` proposal, which overwrites a SKILL.md, only from the CLI with `--yes`; MCP refuses
Reports the rewrite lane's receipts, verdicts and rates over MCP (`brain_skill_rewrite_status`)
limits: Runs no model: drafts and rewrite transcripts come from the calling agent through envelopes
Rewrite checks look at tools, paths, order and output fields, never at prose
Rewrite rounds are scored and staged only from the CLI; MCP reads their status
An interrupted accept of a private proposal is left to a local recovery; a remote one does not name it

features.name: Procedural memory
features.summary: An index of procedures with usage and outcomes, a procedural graph with hints, and recurrence diagnostics.
capabilities: `reconcile` indexes procedure pages, SKILL.md files and runbooks (`*.prompt.md`, `*runbook.md`) with triggers
Walks `Brain/procedures/`, `skills/`, `runbooks/` (or `--root`); reports added, updated and removed entries
Keeps per-entry use count, last use, successes and failures (`mark-used`, MCP `mark_outcome`)
Ranks by success rate on `ranked: true`; entries without outcomes sit at 0.5, then by use count and recency
`procedural-graph rebuild` links procedures, skills, runbooks, proposals to trigger, tag and path-token nodes
Derives a hint projection: per node, the cue tokens of 3+ characters from its title, path, triggers and tags
`brain recurrence` counts support per content hash across scopes: leaning at 3, decided at 5, locked at 8
Adds or removes one source's support in a scope (`brain recurrence learn`, `forget`)
limits: Outcome recording and success ranking are MCP-only; the CLI reconciles, lists and counts uses
The hint projection is read only by `procedural-graph hints` and `brain_procedural_graph`; no hook injects it
Recurrence support is written only by explicit learn, forget and purge calls
